guidance.Malaria: Rest and drink fluids. A malaria test is needed to confirm, so see a clinic.
guidance.Typhoid: Drink safe fluids and eat light meals. Lab testing is needed to confirm.
guidance.Common cold: Rest and fluids usually help. See a professional if it lasts over a week.
guidance.Influenza (flu): Rest, fluids, and paracetamol for discomfort may help. See a doctor if breathing worsens.
guidance.COVID-19 (mild): Rest, isolate where possible, and monitor breathing. Seek care if symptoms worsen.
guidance.Gastroenteritis: Keep hydrated (oral rehydration). Seek care if it lasts over 2 days.
guidance.Pneumonia: Needs medical assessment, especially if breathing is difficult. See a doctor promptly.
guidance.Urinary tract infection: Drink plenty of water. See a doctor, as this usually needs antibiotics.
guidance.Migraine: Rest in a quiet, dark room. See a doctor if attacks are frequent or severe.
guidance.Tension headache: Rest, hydration, and stress relief may help. See a doctor if headaches are frequent.
guidance.Asthma flare-up: Use prescribed inhalers if available. Seek urgent care if breathing does not improve.
guidance.Food poisoning: Keep hydrated with small sips of fluid. Seek care if symptoms are severe or persist.
guidance.Sinusitis: Steam inhalation and fluids may help. See a doctor if it lasts more than 10 days.
guidance.Anaemia: A blood test can confirm this. See a doctor for proper evaluation and diet advice.
guidance.Dehydration: Drink fluids steadily, with oral rehydration salts if available. Seek care if severe.
guidance.Allergic reaction: Avoid the suspected trigger. Seek urgent care if breathing is affected.
guidance.Conjunctivitis: Keep the eye clean and avoid touching it. See a doctor if it does not improve in a few days.
guidance.Ear infection: See a doctor, as this often needs proper examination and possibly antibiotics.
guidance.Hypertension (mild symptoms): See a doctor to have your blood pressure checked properly.
guidance.Type 2 diabetes (warning signs): See a doctor for a blood sugar test as soon as possible.
guidance.Hepatitis (viral): See a doctor promptly for liver function testing.
guidance.Tuberculosis (warning signs): See a doctor promptly for proper testing, especially if symptoms persist for weeks.
guidance.Arthritis: Gentle movement and rest may help. See a doctor for a proper evaluation.
guidance.Anxiety: Relaxation techniques may help. Consider speaking with a counsellor or doctor if it persists.
guidance.Insomnia (stress-related): Good sleep habits may help. See a doctor if it continues for more than a few weeks.
guidance.Constipation: Fluids, fibre, and light activity may help. See a doctor if it persists or is painful.
guidance.Lower back strain: Rest, gentle movement, and avoiding heavy lifting may help. See a doctor if pain persists.
guidance.Premenstrual syndrome (PMS): Often manageable with rest, warmth, and light exercise. See a doctor if it disrupts daily life.
guidance.Dysmenorrhoea (period pain): A warm compress and rest often help. See a doctor if pain is severe or unusual for you.
guidance.Heavy menstrual bleeding: See a doctor, especially if it is a new pattern or causes dizziness or fatigue.
